title: the words before every beginning
hookLine: the words before every beginning — a meal, a drive, an exam
tomorrow: what your prayer is actually saying

cards: Before the first bite of dinner. Before the car pulls out of the driveway. At the top of an exam, before the first answer.
Under the breath, fast, so it's easy to miss: bismillah. Many Muslims have said it since before they could read. It goes before a beginning, so it goes first here too.

teach.h: BI — IN. ISM — NAME. ALLAH — GOD.
ALL BUT ONE SURAH OPENS WITH IT.
teach.b: Bi: in, or with. Ism: name. Allah: God.
In the name of God. Allah isn't the name of a separate god; it's the Arabic word for God, and Arabic-speaking Christians and Jews say it too.
The full line is bismillah ar-rahman ar-rahim: “In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.” All but one of the Qur'an's chapters, called surahs, open with it. So what does it do?
Starting in someone's name means you're not starting alone. It's like working under a name you respect: the work carries that name now, so you want it to be worth carrying.
That's why it goes before small things, not only big ones. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ once told a boy eating beside him: say bismillah, and eat with your right hand.

teach.h: FORGOT? SAY IT WHEN YOU REMEMBER.
teach.b: And for the times you forget, because everyone does, another of his sayings gives a way back in: say it when you remember, in the name of God, at its beginning and its end. Nobody gets locked out of their own lunch.

how: Muslims say bismillah before eating, drinking, setting out, studying and many small daily tasks, and the full line, bismillah ar-rahman ar-rahim, is recited before reading the Qur'an.

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.

s: bismillah is only a grace before meals
it means in the name of God, and it goes before almost any beginning: a meal, a drive, an exam.
Allah is simply the Arabic word for God
Arabic-speaking Christians and Jews say it too.
if you forget it at the start, the moment is lost
a saying of the Prophet ﷺ gives a way back: say it when you remember, in the name of God, at its beginning and its end.

games.q: you sit down to eat, start, and halfway through you realize you forgot to say bismillah. what does the saying of the Prophet ﷺ suggest?
o: stop and start the meal over.
say it now: in the name of God, at its beginning and its end.
it's too late. there's always the next meal.
games.why: say it when you remember. the way back in is built into the practice, because everyone forgets.

games.q: build the word: in + name + God.

practice: One breath with the bell. Think of the very next thing you'll do after this: coffee, an email, the car. Breathe in.
On the way out, say the word for it, aloud or under your breath: bismillah. Or simply give it one full pause before it begins.

wordCard.voice: Bismillah. In the name of God: the words before a beginning, so nothing starts alone. First word on your strand.

orig.note: Arabic: "in the name of God." bi (in) + ism (name) + Allah (God).

carryVoice: Your line: start in the name of. It's why the word comes before a meal, a drive, an exam, and why it came first here. See you tomorrow.
